newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor profit drops on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor profit drops on liquidation.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest car maker, said on Wednesday its 1996 profits were almost halved due to losses from the closure of its Canadian plants and a slowing of the domestic economy.
The flagship unit of the Hyundai Group said net profit for calendar 1996 dropped to 86.8 billion won ($100.7 million) from 156.7 billion won in 1995.
Brisk exports saw sales rise 11 percent to 11.49 trillion won in 1996, up from 10.34 trillion won in 1995, on the sale of 1.31 million vehicles, up from 1.24 million, Hyundai said.

"We had to pay 280 billion won last year to liquidate the plants in Bromont (Canada). Competition on the domestic market was also severe as the economy slowed," said Min Kyong-hwan, a Hyundai spokesman.
Hyundai decided in 1993 to close its Canadian plants with an annual capacity of 100,000 sedans after incurring huge losses. Liquidation was completed last month.
Its domestic sales dropped to 740,349 units in 1996 from 746,070 the year before as consumers cut back on spending on durable goods such as vehicles.
But exports rose to 570,195 units from 491,608.
Analysts said the domestic market was near saturation with little demand from first-time car buyers.

"Price cuts in the form of non-interest installment payments were offered towards the end of last year as domestic sales turned sour," said Hur Gang, an analyst at Hyundai Economic Research Institute.

Competition intensified, particularly in the top end of the market, with the arrival of more imported cars, analysts said. Car imports rose 70 percent in 1996 to about 15,300 units, which accounted for 0.9 percent of the local market.
Analysts said car sales growth would slow further this year as the economy remained in the doldrums.
"Sales conditions look even worse this year," said Lee Kyu-young, an analyst at the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association (KAMA).
He said a weaker yen would make Japanese cars more competitive against Korean products on overseas markets.
Hyundai earlier set its sales target at 13.5 trillion won for this year, or 1.5 million vehicles. It wants to rack up 8.9 trillion won in domestic sales and 4.6 trillion from exports.
A new plant in Turkey will start up in July, making 50,000 compact sedans and minivans each year.
"We will begin marketing new models this year aimed at niche markets. Together with overseas production, they will help boost our sales this year," Min said.
Hyundai's new minivan, Starex, will roll out from March and the sub-compact MX car, which will compete with Daewoo Motor's Tico, will hit the road in the second half of this year. ($1 = 862 won)
